title: Polity: Schedules and parts (Past Year Questions)

questions.q_en: Articles 245 to 255 in Part XI of the Indian Constitution deal with the ____________.
options_en: Financial relations between the Centre and the states
Legislative relations between the Centre and the states
questions.solution_en: Articles 245 to 255 in Part XI of the Indian Constitution deal with legislative relations between the Centre and the States. These articles define the extent of laws made by Parliament and state legislatures, including the distribution of legislative powers under the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.
questions.solution_hi: भारतीय संविधान के भाग XI में अनुच्छेद 245 से 255 केंद्र व राज्यों के बीच विधायी संबंधों से संबंधित हैं। ये अनुच्छेद संघ सूची, राज्य सूची व समवर्ती सूची के अंतर्गत विधायी शक्तियों के वितरण सहित संसद व राज्य विधानसभाओं द्वारा बनाए गए कानूनों की सीमा निर्धारित करते हैं।

questions.q_en: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that a person may be appointed as the Governor of two or more states?
questions.solution_en:
Article 153 of the Indian Constitution states: "Governors of States. - There shall be a Governor for each State: Provided that nothing in this article shall prevent the appointment of the same person as Governor for two or more States."

The proviso allowing the same person to be appointed as Governor for two or more States was added by the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956.

Explanation of Other Options:

• Article 152: Contains the definition of "State" for the purposes of Part VI of the Constitution (which deals with The States), unless the context otherwise requires.

• Article 151: Deals with Audit reports of the Union and the States.

• Article 150: Deals with the Form of accounts of the Union and of the States.

Further insights:

• When a person is appointed as Governor for two or more States, their emoluments and allowances are allocated among the States in such proportion as the President may by order determine (Article 158(3A)).

• This provision allows for flexibility in gubernatorial appointments.
questions.solution_hi:
अनुच्छेद 153 कहता है: "राज्यों के राज्यपाल - प्रत्येक राज्य के लिए एक राज्यपाल होगा: परंतु इस अनुच्छेद की कोई बात एक ही व्यक्ति को दो या अधिक राज्यों के लिए राज्यपाल नियुक्त करने से नहीं रोकेगी।"

एक ही व्यक्ति को दो या अधिक राज्यों का राज्यपाल नियुक्त करने की अनुमति देने वाला प्रावधान 7वें संवैधानिक संशोधन अधिनियम, 1956 द्वारा जोड़ा गया था।

questions.q_en:
Match the following subject matters with their concerned Articles.

ab
1. Superintendence, direction, and control of elections to be vested in an Election commission.A) Article 329
2. Power of parliament to make provisions with respect to election to legislature.B) Article 324
3. Bar of interference by courts in electoral matters.C) Article 327
questions.solution_en:
Article 324 grants the Election Commission the authority to oversee and manage the electoral process.

Article 327 confers upon Parliament the power to enact laws pertaining to the conduct of elections to the legislatures.

Article 329 establishes limitations on judicial interference in electoral matters, maintaining the autonomy of the electoral process.

Hence, correct combination is 1-B, 2-C, 3-A.
questions.solution_hi:
अनुच्छेद 324 चुनाव आयोग को चुनावी प्रक्रिया की देखरेख व प्रबंधन का अधिकार देता है।

अनुच्छेद 327 संसद को विधानसभाओं के चुनाव संचालन से संबंधित कानून बनाने की शक्ति देता है।

अनुच्छेद 329 चुनावी मामलों में न्यायिक हस्तक्षेप पर सीमाएँ स्थापित करता है, जिससे चुनावी प्रक्रिया की स्वायत्तता बनी रहती है।

अतः सही संयोजन दिए गए विकल्प में है।

questions.q_en: The total number of fundamental duties provided by the constitution of India is:
questions.solution_en: The Constitution of India was framed by a Constituent Assembly set up under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946. Originally ten fundamental duties were listed. Later on, by virtue of the 86th Constitution the Amendment in 2002, 11th duty was added.
questions.solution_hi: भारत का संविधान 1946 की कैबिनेट मिशन योजना के अंतर्गत गठित संविधान सभा द्वारा तैयार किया गया था। मूलतः दस मूल कर्तव्य सूचीबद्ध थे। बाद में, 2002 में 86वें संविधान संशोधन के तहत 11वाँ कर्तव्य जोड़ा गया।

questions.q_en: How many languages are included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India as scheduled languages?
questions.solution_en:
The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India originally included 14 languages. Over time, through various constitutional amendments, the number has increased to 22 scheduled languages.

These include: Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Oriya, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, Bodo, Santhali, Maithili, and Dogri.

The 92nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 added Bodo, Santhali, Maithili, and Dogri as the most recent additions.

So, currently, 22 languages are recognized as scheduled languages under the Eighth Schedule.

· Original (1950): 14 languages.

· Current (2024): 22 languages (last addition: Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali in 2003).

· Recent demands: Include Tulu, Rajasthani, Bhojpuri.
questions.solution_hi:
भारतीय संविधान की आठवीं अनुसूची में मूलतः 14 भाषाएँ शामिल थीं। समय के साथ, विभिन्न संवैधानिक संशोधनों के माध्यम से यह संख्या बढ़कर 22 अनुसूचित भाषाएँ हो गई।

इनमें शामिल हैं: असमिया, बंगाली, गुजराती, हिंदी, कन्नड़, कश्मीरी, कोंकणी, मलयालम, मणिपुरी, मराठी, नेपाली, उड़िया, पंजाबी, संस्कृत, सिंधी, तमिल, तेलुगु, उर्दू, बोडो आदि।

questions.q_en: As per article 158, the Governor shall NOT be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State specified in ________ Schedule
questions.solution_en:
According to Article 158(1):

"The Governor shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or a House of the Legislature of any State specified in the First Schedule."

If a person who is already a member of the Parliament or State Legislature is appointed as a Governor, they are deemed to have vacated their seat upon assuming office.
questions.solution_hi:
अनुच्छेद 158(1) के अनुसार:

"राज्यपाल संसद के किसी भी सदन का या प्रथम अनुसूची में निर्दिष्ट किसी राज्य की विधायिका के किसी सदन का सदस्य नहीं होगा।"

यदि पहले से संसद या राज्य विधानसभा का सदस्य रहा कोई व्यक्ति राज्यपाल नियुक्त होता है, तो पद ग्रहण करते ही उसकी सीट रिक्त मानी जाती है।

questions.q_en: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with the election of the Vice President?
questions.solution_en: The election of the Vice President of India is governed by Article 63 to Article 71 under Part V of the Indian Constitution. According to Article 66, the Vice President is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both houses of Parliament using a proportional representation system through a single transferable vote.
questions.solution_hi: भारत के उपराष्ट्रपति के चुनाव को भारतीय संविधान के भाग V के अंतर्गत अनुच्छेद 63 से 71 द्वारा नियंत्रित किया जाता है। अनुच्छेद 66 के अनुसार, उपराष्ट्रपति का चुनाव संसद के दोनों सदनों के सदस्यों से बने एक निर्वाचक मंडल द्वारा एकल संक्रमणीय मत (single transferable vote) के माध्यम से आनुपातिक प्रतिनिधित्व प्रणाली से किया जाता है।

questions.q_en: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that 'The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the state'?
questions.solution_en:
Article 164(2) of the Indian Constitution states: "The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State." This establishes the principle of parliamentary accountability for the state government.

Explanation of Other Options:

• Article 164(3): Requires the Governor to administer the oaths of office and secrecy to a Minister before he enters upon his office.

• Article 164(1): Deals with the appointment of the Chief Minister by the Governor and other Ministers by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister. It also mentions that Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor. Provisos to this clause deal with tribal welfare ministers and limits on the size of the council of ministers.

• Article 164(4): States that a Minister who for any period of six consecutive months is not a member of the Legislature of the State shall at the expiration of that period cease to be a Minister.

Further insights:

• Collective responsibility means that the entire state Council of Ministers is responsible for all its decisions and actions. If the Legislative Assembly passes a no-confidence motion, the entire ministry must resign.

• This principle is analogous to Article 75(3) for the Union Council of Ministers' responsibility to the Lok Sabha.
questions.solution_hi:
अनुच्छेद 164(2) कहता है: "मंत्रिपरिषद राज्य की विधानसभा के प्रति सामूहिक रूप से उत्तरदायी होगी।" यह राज्य सरकार हेतु संसदीय जवाबदेही के सिद्धांत को स्थापित करता है।

अन्य विकल्पों की व्याख्या:

• अनुच्छेद 164(3): राज्यपाल को किसी मंत्री को पद व गोपनीयता की शपथ दिलाने की आवश्यकता है।

questions.q_en: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution is commonly referred to as the 'Magna Carta of India'?
questions.solution_en:
Part III of the Indian Constitution, which deals with Fundamental Rights, is commonly referred to as the 'Magna Carta of India'. The Magna Carta was a charter of rights agreed to by King John of England in 1215, and it is considered a foundational document for constitutional liberties.

Explanation of Other Options:

• Part I: Deals with "The Union and its Territory."

• Part IV: Deals with "Directive Principles of State Policy."

• Part II: Deals with "Citizenship."

Further insights:

• The Fundamental Rights enshrined in Part III (Articles 12 to 35) guarantee basic human rights to all citizens of India, and in some cases, to non-citizens as well.

• These rights are justiciable, meaning they are enforceable by courts.

• They include rights such as the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
questions.solution_hi:
भारतीय संविधान का भाग III, जो मूल अधिकारों से संबंधित है, आमतौर पर 'भारत के मैग्ना कार्टा' के रूप में जाना जाता है। मैग्ना कार्टा 1215 में इंग्लैंड के राजा जॉन द्वारा सहमत अधिकारों का चार्टर था, जिसे संवैधानिक स्वतंत्रताओं हेतु एक आधारभूत दस्तावेज़ माना जाता है।

अन्य विकल्पों की व्याख्या:

• भाग I: "संघ व उसका क्षेत्र" से संबंधित है।

questions.q_en: Which part of the Constitution deals with the Panchayats?
questions.solution_en: Part IX of the Indian Constitution (Articles 243-243O) deals with the Panchayati Raj system. It was introduced through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which established a three-tier local governance structure in rural areas.
questions.solution_hi: भारतीय संविधान का भाग IX (अनुच्छेद 243-243O) पंचायती राज व्यवस्था से संबंधित है। इसे 73वें संवैधानिक संशोधन अधिनियम, 1992 के माध्यम से लागू किया गया, जिसने ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में त्रि-स्तरीय स्थानीय शासन संरचना स्थापित की।

questions.q_en:
_________ Fundamental Duties were added in Part-IV of the Constitution under Article 51-A in the year 1976 through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment.

Options:
questions.solution_en: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976) introduced Ten Fundamental Duties under Article 51-A in Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution. These duties were inspired by the Soviet Constitution and were later increased to Eleven through the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act (2002), which added the duty of parents to provide education to their children.
questions.solution_hi: 42वें संवैधानिक संशोधन अधिनियम (1976) ने भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV-A में अनुच्छेद 51-A के तहत दस मूल कर्तव्य शुरू किए। ये कर्तव्य सोवियत संविधान से प्रेरित थे और बाद में 86वें संवैधानिक संशोधन अधिनियम (2002) के माध्यम से बढ़कर ग्यारह हो गए, जिसने माता-पिता के अपने बच्चों को शिक्षा देने के कर्तव्य को जोड़ा।

questions.q_en: Articles 52 to 78 in Part V of the Indian Constitution deal with __________.
questions.solution_en:
Articles 52 to 78 of the Indian Constitution deal with the Union Executive, which includes:

• President (Article 52-62)

• Vice-President (Article 63-71)

• Prime Minister and Council of Ministers (Article 74-75)

• Attorney General of India (Article 76)
questions.solution_hi:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 52 से 78 संघ की कार्यपालिका से संबंधित हैं, जिसमें शामिल हैं:

• राष्ट्रपति (अनुच्छेद 52-62)

• उपराष्ट्रपति (अनुच्छेद 63-71)

• प्रधानमंत्री व मंत्रिपरिषद (अनुच्छेद 74-75)

• भारत के महान्यायवादी (अनुच्छेद 76)

questions.q_en: In May 2023, the Supreme Court of India granted couples the right to get divorce on the grounds of 'irretrievable breakdown of marriage' under ______ of the Indian Constitution.
questions.solution_en:
· In May 2023, the Supreme Court of India held that it can grant divorce on the grounds of "irretrievable breakdown of marriage" by exercising its extraordinary powers under Article 142(1) of the Constitution.

Article 142(1): Empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any case before it.

· This provision allows the Court to dissolve a marriage even if specific grounds are not met under the Hindu Marriage Act or other personal laws, provided that reconciliation is impossible.

Further Insight:

· This ruling expanded divorce grounds beyond the Hindu Marriage Act, allowing courts to dissolve marriages where reconciliation is impossible.

· Article 132(1): Deals with appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in constitutional matters.

· Article 122(1): Relates to courts not inquiring into parliamentary proceedings.

· Article 152(1): Defines the term "State" for Part VI (not related to judiciary or marriage).
questions.solution_hi:
• मई 2023 में, भारत के सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने कहा कि वह संविधान के अनुच्छेद 142(1) के तहत अपनी असाधारण शक्तियों का प्रयोग कर "विवाह के अपूरणीय विघटन" के आधार पर तलाक दे सकता है।

अनुच्छेद 142(1): सर्वोच्च न्यायालय को किसी भी मामले में पूर्ण न्याय हेतु आवश्यक कोई भी आदेश या डिक्री पारित करने का अधिकार देता है।

questions.q_en: Which Article in the Fundamental Duties is invoked when you see in a private party that the Indian flag has been used as a covering for the speaker's desk?
questions.solution_en: Article 51A (a) of the Indian Constitution states that it is the duty of every citizen "to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem." Using the Indian flag as a decoration or covering violates Flag Code of India and disrespects national symbols.
questions.solution_hi: भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 51A(a) कहता है कि हर नागरिक का कर्तव्य है "संविधान का पालन करना व उसके आदर्शों व संस्थाओं, राष्ट्रीय ध्वज व राष्ट्रगान का सम्मान करना।" भारतीय ध्वज को सजावट या आवरण के रूप में उपयोग करना ध्वज संहिता का उल्लंघन करता है और राष्ट्रीय प्रतीकों का अनादर करता है।

questions.q_en: Article 148 of the Constitution of India provides for an independent office of the ______.
options_en: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
questions.solution_en:
Article 148 - Comptroller and Auditor-General of India

There shall be a Comptroller and Auditor-General of India who shall be appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal and shall only be removed from office in like manner and on like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
questions.solution_hi:
अनुच्छेद 148 - भारत के नियंत्रक व महालेखा परीक्षक (CAG)

भारत का एक नियंत्रक व महालेखा परीक्षक होगा, जिसे राष्ट्रपति द्वारा अपने हस्ताक्षर व मुहर सहित वारंट द्वारा नियुक्त किया जाएगा और उसे केवल उसी तरीके व उन्हीं आधारों पर पद से हटाया जा सकेगा जैसे सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश को।

questions.q_en: Which part of the Constitution of India consists of the idea of a Welfare State?
questions.solution_en: The Directive Principles of State Policy are enumerated in Part IV of the Constitution from Articles 36 to 51. They embody the concept of a welfare state.
questions.solution_hi: राज्य के नीति-निदेशक तत्व भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV में अनुच्छेद 36 से 51 में सूचीबद्ध हैं। ये कल्याणकारी राज्य की अवधारणा को मूर्त रूप देते हैं।

questions.q_en: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions that 'The State shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing that the ownership and control of the material resources of the community are so distributed as best to subserve the common good'?
questions.solution_en: Article 39(b) of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) ensures that material resources are distributed for the common good. It is aimed at achieving economic justice.
questions.solution_hi: राज्य के नीति-निदेशक तत्वों (DPSP) का अनुच्छेद 39(b) यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि भौतिक संसाधनों का वितरण सामान्य भलाई हेतु किया जाए। इसका उद्देश्य आर्थिक न्याय प्राप्त करना है।

questions.q_en: In which of the following years was the citizenship Act passed by the Indian Parliament?
questions.solution_en: The Citizenship Act of 1955 regulates who may acquire Indian citizenship and on what grounds. A person may become an Indian citizen if they are born in India or have Indian parentage or have resided in the country for a period of time, etc. However, illegal migrants are prohibited from acquiring Indian citizenship. An illegal migrant is a foreigner who: (i) enters the country without valid travel documents, like a passport and visa, or (ii) enters with valid documents, but stays beyond the permitted time period.
questions.solution_hi: नागरिकता अधिनियम, 1955 यह नियंत्रित करता है कि कौन भारतीय नागरिकता प्राप्त कर सकता है व किन आधारों पर। कोई व्यक्ति भारतीय नागरिक बन सकता है यदि वह भारत में जन्मा हो, भारतीय वंश का हो या देश में एक निश्चित अवधि तक रहा हो, आदि। हालाँकि, अवैध प्रवासियों को भारतीय नागरिकता प्राप्त करने से प्रतिबंधित किया गया है।

questions.q_en: Which of the following is NOT a condition for acquiring the citizenship of India?
questions.solution_en:
Under the Indian Citizenship Act, 1955, citizenship can be acquired through the following ways:

1) By Birth (Section 3)

2) By Descent (Section 4)

3) By Registration (Section 5)

4) By Naturalisation (Section 6)

5) By Incorporation of Territory (Section 7)

6) By Domicile (Part II of the Constitution)

However, holding property is not a condition for acquiring Indian citizenship. Owning land or assets in India does not automatically grant citizenship.

Further information:

· Descent: If one or both parents are Indian citizens.

· Registration: For PIOs, spouses of Indian citizens, etc., after fulfilling residency requirements.

· Domicile: Permanent residence in India (for certain categories like overseas citizens).
questions.solution_hi:
भारतीय नागरिकता अधिनियम, 1955 के तहत, नागरिकता निम्नलिखित तरीकों से प्राप्त की जा सकती है:

1) जन्म से (धारा 3)

2) वंश से (धारा 4)

3) पंजीकरण से (धारा 5)

4) देशीयकरण (Naturalisation) से (धारा 6)

5) क्षेत्र के समावेशन से (धारा 7)

6) अधिवास (domicile) से (संविधान का भाग II)

questions.q_en: Which of the following articles from the Directive Principles of State Policy mentions the organization of Village Panchayats?
questions.solution_en:
· Article 40 of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) states that the government should take steps to organize village panchayats and empower them to function as self-governing units.

· Article 38 deals with promoting social welfare.

· Article 42 is about securing just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.

· Article 36 defines DPSP but does not specifically mention Panchayats.
questions.solution_hi:
• राज्य के नीति-निदेशक तत्वों (DPSP) का अनुच्छेद 40 कहता है कि सरकार को ग्राम पंचायतों का संगठन करना चाहिए व उन्हें स्वशासी इकाइयों के रूप में कार्य करने हेतु सशक्त बनाना चाहिए।

• अनुच्छेद 38 सामाजिक कल्याण को बढ़ावा देने से संबंधित है।

• अनुच्छेद 42 न्यायसंगत व मानवीय कार्य दशाओं व प्रसूति राहत सुनिश्चित करने से संबंधित है।

• अनुच्छेद 36 DPSP को परिभाषित करता है।
